newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Detained group "wanted to help rebuild Bosnia".
newsitem.headline: Detained group "wanted to help rebuild Bosnia".

text.p: A group of men from Iraq and Jordan who have been detained in Sarajevo as illegal immigrants claimed to have been recruited to help rebuild post-war Bosnia, a NATO source said on Friday.
Bosnian police arrested 24 Iraqis and four Jordanians when they arrived in Sarajevo on September 29 aboard a Jordanian cargo aircraft which was not officially carrying passengers.
They are being held by police in refugee accommodation and Bosnian authorities have not said what they intend to do with them.
The incident has embarrassed NATO peacekeepers who allowed the group to leave Sarajevo airport without passport or customs checks.
The NATO source, who refused to be identified, said the Iraqis told Bosnian authorities they had answered a newspaper advertisement in Jordan for people to work on Bosnia's reconstruction.
"Their intentions once they got to Bosnia are still unknown but it's obvious there is an illegal immigrant scam going on," he added.
People in the Sarajevo suburb where the new arrivals were being held said the men were frightened to go home and wanted political asylum.
A Jordanian official said the Bosnian government had been asked to explain the detention of the Jordanian citizens since they did not need visas to enter Bosnia.
